sentences.text:
In these two appeals, the appellants have challenged the judgment and award dated 23.09.2014 passed in M.V.C.No.1770/2012 on the file of the Fast Track Court and Additional M.A.C.T., Hassan (for short 'the Tribunal').
2. For the sake of convenience, the parties shall be referred with respect to their status before the Tribunal.
3. Briefly stated the facts are, the husband of petitioner No.1, father of petitioner Nos.2 and 3 and son of petitioners No.4 and 5 by name Suresha @ Suryanarayana, the deceased, while walking on the left side of the road near Railway Station on B.M.Road, Hassan, a motor bike bearing No.KA- 50/K-4632 came behind and dashed against him inflicting him severe head injury bringing him down to unconscious state.
He was taken to Government Hospital, Hassan and he was admitted to NIMHANS, NC: 2023:KHC:29508 Bangalore.

Thereafter to SDM Ayurvedic Hospital, Hassan,
Government Hospital, Hassan, Bowring Hospital, Bangalore and was discharged on 24.11.2012.
Ultimately, on 05.12.2012, he was succumbed to death on account of the injuries.
The deceased has filed the claim under Section 166 of the M.V.Act through his wife as guardian.
After his death, his legal representatives have come on record.
Claim was opposed by the owner and insurer of the motor cycle.

4. The Tribunal after recording the evidence of the parties and by the impugned judgment allowed the claim petition awarding compensation of Rs.9,89,000/- with interest @ 8% per annum with a direction to the respondents to deposit the compensation.

Aggrieved by the same, the Insurance Company has filed M.F.A.No.772/2015 whereas, the petitioners pleading inadequacy of NC:
2023:KHC:29508 compensation and seeking enhancement have filed M.F.A.No.7301/2015 on various grounds.

5. Heard the arguments of Sri.Girish B.Baladare, learned counsel for the petitioners and Sri.O.Mahesh, learned Counsel for the Insurance Company.
6.

It is the contention of the learned counsel for the Insurance Company that there was no accident,
the deceased was found lying in the Railway Station, Hassan; there is a delay of 19 days in filing the complaint, when the deceased was taken to NIMHANS, Bangalore, on 11.02.2012, the history was furnished by his wife as 'found unconscious in the Railway Station, Hassan'.
The deceased obtained the wound certificate on 01.08.2012 by physically appearing before the hospital, five months after the accident.
Contrarily, it is the case of the petitioners that the deceased was unconscious from the date of accident till his death.

When the NC: 2023:KHC:29508 deceased was brought to the hospital through 108 Ambulance, attendant was one Laxman, the reason for brining him and the history, so also the wound certificate create a doubt.

In the wound certificate, no vehicle number is forthcoming; the hospital records have been tampered; the accident details were not made known to anybody; PW-1/Sumitra is the wife of the deceased, she is not an eye-witness, PW-2/Rangaswamy,
the so-called eye-witness has not given any complaint to the Police, if really he was an eye-witness,

4

sentences.text: why he has not filed the complaint finds no reason.
He further submitted that the deceased himself had presented the claim petition on 16.11.2012 seeking compensation through his wife as guardian as he was in Coma.
As he succumbed to death on 05.12.2012, the petition came to be amended impleading the petitioners as dependants of the deceased.
Referring to Ex.R3/MLC register extract, it is further contended that there is a clear mention of 'influence of alcohol', but the Tribunal ignored the same.
In Ex.P10/Postmortem report, the Doctor has opined that 'deceased died due to septaecemic shock and complications of injuries sustained earlier'.
There is no reference of accidental injuries.

The deceased having consumed alcohol died in the Railway Station; 19 days thereafter, the motor cycle has been implicated; false complaint was filed to the Police, claim made is fishy, there is a fraud played, there is no bonafides in the conduct of the petitioners and it is a fit case for dismissal.
7.
Per contra, learned counsel for the petitioners has contended that on 11.02.2012, soon after the accident, the deceased fell unconscious.
No family members were found near him.

Since he was hit by motor cycle, one Laxman carried him to the S.C.Hospital, Hassan and thereafter on the very day,
NC: 2023:KHC:29508 he was shifted to NIMHANS, Bangalore.
He was inpatient till 30.03.2012.
If there is any self-fall injury, a person will not sustain such an injury, which will make him to hospitalize for more than one month at NIMHANS, Bangalore.

After discharge from the NIMHANS,
the deceased was admitted to various hospitals as inpatient till 24.11.2012.
Only after discharge, he died within ten days and the medical records clearly point out that the deceased died on account of the accidental injuries.

When the petitioner No.1 and her family members were struggling to save the life of the deceased in NIMHANS, Bangalore, there was no occasion for them to immediately go to Police Station to file the compliant and for this reason, the delay of 19 days has occurred.
When the deceased was brought to the hospital, there is a clear report that he was hit by a bike.

The records maintained in the S.C.Hospital, Hassan clearly point out that on 11.02.2012 at 3.45 p.m., the deceased was hit by a - 10 - NC: 2023:KHC:29508 bike as he was a pedestrian near Railway Station.
This establishes the accident.
The contention of the Insurance Company on the basis of entries made in NIMHANS is not correct.

If the deceased was found unconscious in the Railway Station, the Railway Police ought to have come to his aid and they could have taken him to the hospital, but there is no such situation as the accident took place on B.M.Road near Railway Station.

Hence, the contention taken by the Insurance Company is not proper, the Insurance Company is trying to mislead the Court by referring to certain entries made in NIMHANS, which is said to have been given by the wife of the deceased.

When some other person carried the deceased to S.C.Hospital, Hassan, it clearly goes to show that the patient was a pedestrian and he was hit by motor cycle in question near Railway Station, there is no question of informing the NIMHANS on the next day morning that he was found unconscious in the Railway Station.

When there is no proper - 11 - Mrs Sumithra vs The Manager on 18 August, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/46765931/
5 NC: 2023:KHC:29508 evidence to show that on whose instigation such an entry has been made, the entry made in S.C.Hospital, Hassan within 10 minutes of the accident, is relevant and therefore, the Tribunal has rightly accepted the materials placed on behalf of the petitioners to prove the accident.
7.1. The contention as regards consumption of alcohol has no basis as in the PM report, there is any mention that alcohol contents were traced in the intestine of the dead body.
7.2.

sentences.text: It is further contended that the deceased was an agriculturist, doing pipeline work earning more than Rs.10,000/- per month.
Even in Lok Adalat, a sum of Rs.7,000/- is being considered as notional income for a person with no proof of income in the year 2012.
But the Tribunal has taken the income at Rs.6,000/-, proper compensation is not awarded under the conventional heads and he sought for enhancement of compensation.
I have given my anxious consideration to the arguments addressed on behalf of the parties and perused the records.
9. There are two points involved in these matters, (i) genuineness of the accident; (2) quantum of compensation awarded by the Tribunal.

10. As regards the genuineness of the accident is concerned, the Insurance Company is seriously disputing that the deceased was found unconscious in the Railway Station, Hassan, he was brought to the Hospital from Railway Station, 19 days thereafter, motor cycle in question was placed against him that it has caused the accident.
The material on record did point out that at 3.45 p.m. on 11.02.2012, the deceased was brought to S.C.Hospital, Hassan (District Hospital) with a history of accident hit by a bike.

From there, he was hospitalized to NIMHANS till 30.03.2012, he was under hospitalization at SDM Ayurvedic Hospital,
- 13 - NC: 2023:KHC:29508 Hassan till 15.04.2012; he was in Government Hospital, Hassan till 15.05.2012; he was inpatient in Bowring Hospital till 24.11.2012 and after discharge, he was brought back home and on 5.12.2012 he is reported to be dead.
11.
It was argued that there was a specific mention of alcohol which has not been clarified before the Tribunal.
On perusal of Ex.R3/wound certificate, it is seen that four words have been stricken off and there are some entries referring to accident and it also refers to the bike No.KA-50-K- 4632.
The author of Ex.R3 has not been brought before the Tribunal.

Ex/R4 is the NIMHANS Emergency Case Record where it refers that, first petitioner Sumithra (wife) has brought the injured to the NIMHANS with further reference that 'Alleged history of patient found unconscious at Railway Station' and this is the one important aspect the Mrs Sumithra vs The Manager on 18 August, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/46765931/
6 - 14 - NC: 2023:KHC:29508 Insurance Company is banking upon to dispute the alleged incident.
12.
As per the records, one Laxman has brought the deceased to the Government Hospital, Hassan immediately after the accident.
Before the hospital authorities, it is informed the history of the accident; the patient was unconscious till his death.
The submission of Sri O.Mahesh regarding the deceased visiting Government Hospital on 01.08.2012 to obtain the injury certificate is explained misreading of 'SCH' as 'Self'.
It is clarified by Sri Baladare, learned counsel that in fact 'SCH' is 'Sri Chamarajendra Hospital'.
This contention of Sri.O.Mahesh can find explanation in the wound certificate.
No doubt, the deceased was unconscious from the date of accident till the date of his death.
He was hospitalized at various hospitals.
But the issue is, who gave the information to S.C.Hospital, Hassan and NIMHANS, Bangalore regarding history - 15 - NC: 2023:KHC:29508 of accident.
If the deceased was found unconscious in Railway Station, this might have been within the knowledge of the Railway Authorities.
Only these are the doubts, which are clarified by the petitioners.
However, the contention urged by the Insurance Company that the deceased was found at Railway Station or it was a case of accident on B.M.Road in front of Railway station has to be clarified.
13. I have carefully perused the impugned judgment.
The contentions raised by the Insurance Company has not been addressed by the Tribunal.
The Police papers have been simply accepted and the Tribunal has not gone into all these aspects, but it has decided the claim as it is a simple claim petition and assessed the compensation.
The Tribunal has taken Rs.6,000/- as notional income even though in the year 2012, the notional income is assessed at Rs.7,000/-.

Hence, the assessment of compensation is guided in the judgment of the - 16 - NC: 2023:KHC:29508 Hon'ble Apex Court in National Insurance Co.Ltd.
-vs- Pranay Sethi and Others1, so also the principle of multiplier in Sarla Varma (Smt.) and Others -vs- Delhi Transport Corporation and Another2 and those principles have to be adopted by the Tribunal.

National Insurance Co.Ltd.
-vs- Pranay Sethi and Others1
entities.label: PRECEDENT

entities.text: Sarla Varma (Smt.) and Others -vs- Delhi Transport Corporation and Another2
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Hence, when the doubts raised by the Insurance Company are not clarified as seen from the material on record, I feel it appropriate that the matter requires re-consideration on these aspects and therefore, the Tribunal is required to examine the aspect of the accident in the background of doubt expressed by the Insurance Company, also observation made above and to decide the case on merits afresh.
Accordingly, point Nos.1 and 2 are answered.

14. The appeal filed by the petitioners for enhancement of compensation needs to be dismissed in the background of remand and the (2017) 16 SCC 680 (2009) 6 SCC 121 Mrs Sumithra vs The Manager on 18 August, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/46765931/
7 - 17 - NC: 2023:KHC:29508 appeal filed by the Insurance Company has to be allowed in part.

15. In the result, the following:
ORDER (i) M.F.A.No.772/2015 is allowed in part.
(ii) M.F.A.No.7301/2015 is dismissed.
(iii) The impugned judgment and award is set aside.
(iv) The matter is remanded back to the Tribunal restoring the claim petition to the stage of further evidence of the petitioners.

Petitioners shall lead evidence by examining relevant witnesses including the Railway Authorities to explain the accident and cause of death of the deceased and to determine the quantum of compensation afresh in accordance with law.

- 18 - NC: 2023:KHC:29508 (v) Opportunity shall also be provided to the Insurance Company to lead further evidence;
vi) Without further notice, the parties shall appear before the Tribunal on 18th September, 2023.
vii) The amount in deposit, if any, shall be transmitted to the Tribunal, along with records.
